desc: Implement coordinate compression for all start and end points of the intervals to map large values to small ranks.
Sort the intervals by their start times while keeping track of their original indices.
Precompute a suffix maximum array `suffix_max[k][rank]` representing the maximum total weight achievable by selecting `k` non-overlapping intervals starting after a given time rank.

Write a recursive DFS function that selects up to 4 non-overlapping intervals, using the precomputed suffix maximums for pruning, and tracks the solution with the maximum weight and lexicographically smallest index list.
Return the best index list found after the DFS completes.
Verify the logic for `S[k][i]` calculation (AT MOST k vs EXACTLY k) and ensure the DFS correctly handles the case where the optimal solution uses fewer than 4 intervals.
Test edge cases: single interval, no valid non-overlapping set of size > 1, all intervals overlapping, large coordinates.
Verify time complexity: Sorting $O(N \log N)$, Suffix computation $O(N)$, DFS with pruning $O(N \cdot 4)$ (effectively linear in practice due to pruning and small depth). Total $O(N \log N)$.
